title: Learning to see the Earth differently
story: My PhD began at Sharif in 2013. My early introduction to GIS and remote sensing gave me a new way to ask questions about water. I started with ArcGIS and began learning MATLAB.

title: Turning an idea into a product
story: Alongside my PhD, I co-founded a company in 2015. Courses on entrepreneurship helped us move from ideas to products and minimum viable products. I designed website experiences for satellite-based agricultural monitoring and rural tourism, using PowerPoint to prototype interfaces and create presentation videos. We dissolved the company in 2019, but the design and communication skills stayed with me.
outcome: Product concepts, two website UX designs and presentation videos.

title: From scripts to reusable models
story: In Italy, I strengthened my MATLAB skills while processing satellite imagery. I learned to build models, write functions and assemble reusable components into modular software. Coding became a way to develop and test scientific ideas.

title: Learning by explaining
story: Teaching at Sharif gave me another way to work with ideas: explain them clearly, organize them into a course and help others develop their own understanding.
outcome: University teaching alongside my doctoral research.

title: Carrying the experience forward
story: I completed my PhD in 2019. The same year, our company closed. Research, coding and product design had become connected parts of my experience, ready to carry into the next stage.
outcome: A PhD and experience spanning research, software and product design.

title: From satellite data to land models
story: My first postdoctoral role introduced me to the VIC model, land surface modeling and data assimilation. I began working in Ubuntu and Linux, using the command line and Bash scripts. I used MATLAB to preprocess satellite data and prepare model inputs.
outcome: Satellite data prepared for modeling and assimilation experiments.

title: Making knowledge accessible online
story: In 2020 and 2021, I taught at Amirkabir University and learned Google Earth Engine while teaching a master’s course. Teaching through the pandemic also meant learning to record lessons, which led me to start a YouTube channel. In 2021, I became a faculty member at the Research Institute for Earth Sciences, before moving to the United States.
outcome: Online lessons, a YouTube channel and an Earth-science faculty role.

title: Scaling up—and moving to Python
story: At Michigan State, I was introduced to high-performance computing. My online master’s studies in analytics at Georgia Tech also helped me learn Python. I moved from MATLAB toward Python, building confidence with NumPy and pandas, then expanding into machine learning with scikit-learn and PyTorch.
outcome: Larger computing workflows and a growing Python and machine-learning toolkit.

title: Building research software and global products
story: At NASA, I deepened my use of Git and GitHub, developed within NASA’s Land Information System (LIS) using Fortran, and learned to build Python software packages through AgroTrack. I developed my first global soil-moisture product using machine learning. The work expanded both the scientific questions I could tackle and the software skills I needed to answer them.
outcome: A global machine-learning soil-moisture product and reusable research software.

title: From foundation models to agents
story: More recently, I have learned to fine-tune geospatial foundation models and benchmark them against one another. I am also exploring agents to automate everyday work, from software development to building this website and maintaining its research information. Each new need becomes a reason to learn the next skill.
outcome: Foundation-model experiments and automation for research and everyday development.
